From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T08:32:00Z
Subject: Weekly bridge brief — QBR primer and immediate asks

Morning team —

Quick standalone brief to align on this week’s leadership cadence ahead of the QBR dry run on Friday. I pulled the attached heatmap and a draft one-pager for the exec slide. High level below (short & actionable):

WINS
- Hosted API latency improvements: p95 down 12% week-over-week after runtime kernel tweak; customers on Dedicated reporting smoother tail latencies.
- New Marketplace listing (Elliott Tech) completed technical validation yesterday — onboarding scheduled.

RISKS
- Capacity: two Dedicated pools show rising queuing for long-context workloads (models >16k). If traffic trends continue, we’ll breach the soft SLO for mid-December.
- QBR readiness: product heatmap still missing the compliance cost impact slide (needed for finance & legal).

ASKS (for this afternoon / EOD where possible)
1) Soojin — can your team produce the capacity mitigation plan (3 options with RTO and cost delta) by 4pm? I’ll use the one-pager for the slides.
2) Laura — need a single slide with the compliance/cost tradeoffs and ask for a confirmation: are we summarizing retention & audit-log costs as ‘Ongoing’ or ‘Material one-time’?
3) Karthik — quick OKR check: share latest cross-team risks for Model Onboarding (Objective 2) so we can include callouts.
4) Vanessa/Marissa — confirm whether the Elliott marketplace onboarding can be included as a customer success win on the QBR intro (they’ve signed the integration PO).

Attachments: weekly-ops-heatmap.pdf, qbr-onepager-v2.pptx

I’ll consolidate replies into the QBR primer doc by 5pm. Thanks —

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Thanks Jordan. A couple of quick clarifications:

- Compliance cost framing: Finance prefers to call the increased audit-log retention an "operational uplift" unless we have a clear one-time migration cost. At this point, present as 'Ongoing incremental cost' with a $/month estimate. I'll draft the slide.

- Capacity mitigation: we should include a conservative forecast for holiday traffic. Soojin, if you can include a holiday scenario (+20% traffic for two weeks) that will help the execs decide on burst vs reserved purchase.

I’ll attach the compliance slide to my reply in 90 minutes. If finance needs different language, flag it and I’ll iterate.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Looping the OKR status in brief:

Objective 2 — Model Onboarding (Owner: ML Onboarding)
- Current status: 2/5 integrations on track; 2 delayed due to data schema gating; 1 in discovery.
- Key risk: schema variation across partners is causing rework; estimated impact is a 3-week delay on two integrations.
- Mitigation: we’ve started a schema-mapping kit (proto) and an integration checklist; need support from Platform infra for a temporary mapping lambda (ETA: 7 days if prioritized).

Ask: Jordan/So & Platform infra — can we prioritize the mapping lambda as a P1 for next sprint to avoid pushing two integrations into the next quarter? If yes, I’ll mark the dependency in the QBR packet and include the delta.

Short note on Elliott Tech: legal review is in the final pass; procurement asked for a copy of our SOC 2 attestation — Laura, can you confirm the link we share?

— Karthik
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T15:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Weekly bridge brief — QBR primer and immediate asks

Quick update on capacity and the requested artifacts:

- Capacity mitigation plan: attached summary (weekly-ops-heatmap.pdf includes the three-option plan):
  Option A (short-term burst): enable burst pools in us-west, expected cost +18% month-to-month, RTO immediate (config change).
  Option B (reserved GPUs): reserve additional capacity in Dedicated pool, cost +9% committed monthly but lowers p95 under sustained load.
  Option C (hybrid with quantized variants): short-term fallback to quantized variant for large-context requests, quality delta <3% on our eval set, implementation ~10 days.

- Holiday scenario tested (+20% for two weeks) shows Option B keeps SLOs stable but Option A is cheapest to start quickly.

- SOC2 link for procurement: https://redwood.app/security/SOC2-report-2026 (Laura — please confirm this is the public attestation we want to share).

Vanessa/Marissa — on Elliott: they signed the integration PO; we can list the customer win in the intro if legal gives the go-ahead (Procurement has the attestation link).

I’ll incorporate any language tweaks and hand the one-pager back to Jordan by 5pm for the QBR deck.

— Soojin
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference
